notes:
Civil-war state Cliopatria lacks (new_slug osroes-i; type rebel, rule 5: a rival Parthian king with half the empire for nineteen years). Pages opened: Osroes I of Parthia, Vologases III.

COUNTERPART EVENTS MISSING: the parthian-empire dossier (written by me-06-a) treats Parthia as one state throughout 110-129 and draws the Cliopatria Parthian shapes; it needs a loss of the western half to osroes-i in 110, and the matching gain in 129 (and its occupation_start by Rome in 116 should name the Osroes land). The Cliopatria Parthian shapes may already contain the west for these years; if so, the renderer should subtract Babylonia for 110-129.

UNSETTLED: the extent of the west (the page says 'including Mesopotamia' and omits Media; Upper Mesopotamia, Susiana and Media are not claimed); the start (revolt 109, reign from 110); Parthamaspates (116-117) is a Roman client, not entered as a state; the contender Mithridates V (129/130-140) held no land named on the pages; the Mithridates IV rivalry of c. 129-147 was not opened. Gazetteer: all names resolve.

ROUTE TO roman-empire (eu-04) and parthian-empire (me-06-a): their occupation pairs (roman-empire /ledger/70-71, 115 and 117; parthian-empire /ledger/53-54, 116 and 117) name parthian-empire and roman-empire; the owner of Babylonia in 116-117 is osroes-i, so the counterpart should be osroes-i (or the pair mirrored with it), and parthian-empire needs the 110 loss and 129 gain of the west. The Roman start is 115 in roman-empire against 116 on the Osroes I page (Seleucia and Ctesiphon fell in 116). (2) Blocking finding, the Characene overlap: all Babylonia components (keyframe, found, dissolve, both occupation events, predecessor and successor land, both war zones) are now Babylonia minus Al-Basrah and Maysan, the reviewer's fix (verified: the resulting shape shares 0 cells with the characene keyframe, which also holds Kuwait; Kuwait is not in Babylonia). (3) Confidence 2 on the first three events was applied by the reviewer and is kept. (4) Thin item, the start year: the Osroes I lead says he 'ruled the western portion of the Parthian Empire from 109 to 129, with a one-year interruption' and the Vologases III page has '(r. 109-129)' inline, but the same pages date his revolt to 109 against Pacorus II (r. 78-110) and give the reign of Vologases III as 110 to 147; the earlier read of the Osroes I page had '110-129: He ruled the western part of the empire, including Mesopotamia'. I keep 110, the year the page's succession line gives for ruling the west, since 109 is the revolt and Pacorus II was still king; DISAGREEMENT with the reviewer's 'consider 109': no page says he held land in 109. The one-year interruption in the lead is Trajan's 116-117, which the dossier now draws as an occupation.
